nodes.title: Learning module (harness2-style Propose -> Probe -> Compose, per tenant): learning.propose, proposal.probe, proposal.accept (A2), experiment.start (A2, shadow A/A first), experiment.assign, experiment.check (hazard stop + A3 revert, verdict only at the horizon), experiment.stop; wins go to deployment.split (100% treatment on the binding) as an A2 card; job learning.check every minute, never auto-published.

A learning proposal may only change an allowlist of editable components (opening.usefulFirst, objection approaches, goal descriptions, persona notes, fact order, tool guidance, maxSilenceS/maxTurns); the rest of the agent is checked as an empty diff on the resolved config, plus provenance (no number/URL absent from facts), manipulation and never-say lints, the shared safety lint and reply door.
nodes.rationale: Blueprint learning.md §2 'never learned' list; locking is enforced on the resolved config, not trusted from the op list.
nodes.reverse_if: The owner wants learning to touch other parts (e.g. register sliders after a listener panel), or a red-team set shows a locked change escaping the empty-diff check.

nodes.title: The shadow A/A gate judges the false-winner rate by its one-sided 99% Wilson lower bound against 6.5%, not the point estimate.
nodes.rationale: measure.2026-10-21.aa-point-estimate-false-fail: the point estimate breached 6.5% on 2-6% of clean datasets from Monte Carlo noise alone, which would block healthy tenants.
nodes.reverse_if: Live tenants' A/A rates sit between 6.5% and the bound often enough to let a genuinely miscalibrated procedure through, or the run count rises enough that the point estimate is precise.

nodes.title: Shadow A/A with 1,000 re-randomisations on clean iid data (30% success): point estimate > 6.5% in 3/100, 2/100, 6/100 salts at n = 120/300/1,000 (mean 5.0-5.2%, max 7.3%); with the 99% Wilson lower bound 0/300 false fails; clustered units (60 contacts counted 10x) fail 50/50 (54% false winners).
nodes.method: shadowAA() in product/server/modules/learning/stats.ts, 100 salts per size plus 50 clustered, scratch script in the coding sandbox, synthetic data

nodes.title: Learning module tests: 21/21 pass (after the integrator contract changes), 2 consecutive runs (9 known-answer stats incl. Fleiss power reproducing the blueprint's 1,565/686/2,036/1,094/6,510/14,751 per arm; 10 Postgres tests: gates, probe regression, A2 accept with calls-to-prove, A/A plumbing fail and pass, no-peeking, win -> A2 deployment.split card, start refuses without version.candidate, background job, hazard stop -> A3 revert, safety stop, no cross-workspace pooling). Cross-module test with calls-shaped conversations (END_OPTED_OUT, goal_values outcomes, NULL untrusted outcomes) shows both the hazard stop and the decision firing.
nodes.method: node --import tsx --test tests/learning*.test.ts on the throwaway cluster (vp_mod_learning); sibling tools faked

nodes.title: Learning calls agents tools agreed with the integrator on 2026-10-21 but not yet registered: test.simulate_batch {agentId, config, simCallerIds, seeds} -> {runs}; version.candidate {agentId, config, parentVersionId, note} -> {versionId, number, versionHash, brief}; deployment.revert_to_last_good {agentId, binding} (A3). Winners go to deployment.split (A2, registered). The dialer must call experiment.assign; calls also call experiment.check per connected call.
nodes.closes_when: The agents, calls and campaigns modules register these tools with matching shapes and an integration test runs propose -> probe -> accept -> start -> check across real modules.

nodes.title: Learning's success metric uses each business's outcome_definition.goal_values (never a literal) and counts only contacts with a recorded outcome (verified, manager, or a trusted judge's guess); guardrails use catalogue reason codes END_OPTED_OUT, CONV_COMPLAINT, END_CRISIS on every live contact.
nodes.rationale: The calls builder found the earlier defaults ('success', 'opt_out'/'complaint') matched nothing calls writes, which silently disabled the decision and the hazard stop; untrusted AI guesses must never feed experiments (blueprint F4).
nodes.reverse_if: Calls changes where outcomes or reason codes live, or a validated leading indicator is approved as a primary metric for a tenant.

nodes.title: Rejected: gating the shadow A/A on outcome-coverage imbalance across the shadow split (two-proportion p < 0.01).
nodes.tried: shadowAA() failed the plumbing check when the share of calls with an outcome differed between the two hash-split shadow arms at p < 0.01.
nodes.broke: The shadow arms are a hash of the contact id, so a real outcome-writer bug cannot correlate with them. The gate fired only by chance: 13 of 2,000 healthy datasets (150 contacts, 20 without an outcome). Each firing left the experiment unlaunched (aa_failed plus an issue), and it was the likely cause of the learning CI flake at 7bec779. The overall coverage floor is kept; the imbalance p is still reported.

nodes.title: Shadow A/A on healthy synthetic history (150 contacts, 30 successes, 20 without an outcome, random ids and salts): the coverage-imbalance gate fired 13/2,000 (runs 200) and 6/1,000 (runs 1,000). With the gate removed, 0/1,000 shadow A/A runs failed. Afterwards learning.test.ts passed 30/30 in a loop and the full suite passed 284/284 twice on one shared database.
nodes.method: shadowAA() in product/server/modules/learning/stats.ts, scratch script in the coding sandbox; node --test loops

events.details: Learning module built in product/server/modules/learning (migration 0801); 19/19 tests green; A/A gate switched to a Wilson lower bound after measuring point-estimate false fails.
